paragraphs: The morning begins with fueling vehicles and verifying meters and product types. Midday brings vehicle washing, care, and equipment adjustment. Before peak traffic, attendants inspect pump meters and make corrections. Afternoons include vessel supply and docking assistance. Before leaving, they reconcile inventory and accounts for the next day's peak.

Employment is projected to decline to 99,000 by 2034, a net decrease of about 1,000 jobs, with roughly 14,400 openings per year. Median annual pay was about $34,800 in 2026 (BLS OOH, 2026).

AI will not replace service attendants, but it will reduce basic roles. Self-service fueling and car washes speed up routine tasks, shifting attendants from operating fuel nozzles toward vessel supply, on-site assistance, equipment maintenance, and customer service. Mechanical service alone faces pressure, while people who can assist effectively on site become more valuable.

paragraphs: A score of 4/10, low-moderate, reflects exposure in vehicle and watercraft service. Self-service accelerates basic fueling, while people remain responsible for supply and assistance.

Low-moderate exposure does not mean high risk. Mechanical fueling tasks face replacement, not on-site assistance roles. Attendants who work effectively on site and supply vessels become scarcer as efficiency rises. Roles limited to holding a fuel nozzle face the greatest pressure.
Start in service work and build equipment and on-site skills. Pure fueling roles are shrinking in the AI era, so develop assistance skills early.
Advance from operating a nozzle to managing supplies + maintaining equipment. Learn basic operations and work toward station manager.
Emphasize customer service and on-site experience, and identify the stations where you have worked. Employers value reliability and diligence.
Do not assess candidates only on diligence. Test practical judgment on site. Experienced attendants who can supply vessels justify performance incentives.
